nodes.label: Hand-Rolled MVVM (No Framework)
nodes.rationale: Standard MVVM with no CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and no DI container — ObservableObject, RelayCommand and a few helpers in Common/ are the entire framework, intentionally hand-rolled; everything is new'd directly.

nodes.label: Shared Performance Sampler
nodes.rationale: CPU/Memory/Storage/Network tabs are thin compositions over one shared PerformanceViewModel because all their data comes from one HardwareMonitorService.Sample() call per tick — giving each tab its own timer would mean redundant PerformanceCounter instantiation for identical data.

nodes.label: On-Demand vs Polled Convention
nodes.rationale: Anything beyond a trivial registry/perf-counter read (event-log scans, recursive file-system walks, registry sweeps, network calls) is gated behind an explicit button, never added to a per-tick timer.

nodes.label: Three-Level Navigation (Groups/Tabs/Sections)
nodes.rationale: Three nested TabControls with deliberately different shapes so a glance tells which level you are on. Sections exist because tabs grew to 91 stacked cards in one unbroken scroll; wrapping card runs in section TabItems needs no ViewModel change, unlike the bool-per-section switching DevicesDriversView still uses. All three levels share one strip ControlTemplate parameterized via attached properties.

nodes.label: SelectTabByName Resolver
nodes.rationale: Walks TabItem.Content, not the visual tree (a TabControl only realizes the selected tab's content), breadth-first so a group beats a same-named leaf, then normalizes below the match to its first leaf. Every leaf tab keeps its original header text because that text is the address used by --tab, Ctrl+1..9, the Ctrl+K palette and every cross-tab jump; the optional section argument extends the address to tab-then-section.

nodes.label: Live Theming via DynamicResource
nodes.rationale: ApplyPalette runs colors through ColorMath.AdjustSaturation and overwrites palette brush keys directly in Application.Current.Resources — this only works because every consumer references those keys via DynamicResource; a StaticResource consumer silently stops re-theming. Palette colors must clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 against their family's three surfaces, and ThemeViewModel.Palettes is the runtime authority over Dark.xaml's literals.

nodes.label: Glow+Core Chart Series Pair
nodes.rationale: Every history chart is a pair of LineSeries sharing one ObservableCollection — a thick translucent glow stroke drawn first, then a crisp 2px core stroke with gradient fill. SkiaSharp paints live outside WPF's resource system, so recoloring (and legend text theming via ChartTheme.ThemedLegend) is done in code.

nodes.label: Registry Change Journal
nodes.rationale: Append-only log (registry-changes.json) of registry writes the app makes on the user's behalf, with per-entry programmatic undo and export-as-.reg of the prior state. Deliberately not wired into every registry-writing call — when touching an unjournaled write path, prefer routing it through the journal, but don't treat absence elsewhere as a bug to fix in an unrelated change.

nodes.label: Confirm-Backup-Revert Pattern
nodes.rationale: A registry or wevtutil-style write that isn't purely additive gets an explicit Yes/No confirmation stating the exact change and its cost, pre-change values backed up to a small JSON file, and a one-click revert command — reference implementation is WerReportService's LocalDumps toggle.

nodes.label: Bundled Resource + User Override
nodes.rationale: EventKnowledgeBaseService loads a read-only embedded EventKnowledgeBase.json keyed by provider|eventId, then merges a user-editable overrides file on top — a curated dataset ships with the app yet stays user-extensible without a rebuild; reusable anywhere that shape is needed.

nodes.label: Maintained Reference Lists (Embedded Seed to Settings Copy)
nodes.rationale: A curated, updatable-without-a-rebuild reference list (the pool tag dictionary, the known-problem-driver list) ships as an embedded resource and is copied to AppPaths.SettingsDirectory on first use; the service then always reads the settings-dir copy so a user or future update mechanism can replace it without a rebuild. Both lists are explicitly labelled curated/partial, never a complete authority.

nodes.label: Quick Flag, Not a Verdict
nodes.rationale: Heuristics are explicitly documented in code and UI as informational only: pattern-matches on ambiguous data, undocumented bitmask/registry conventions, and outdated-driver/BIOS-age checks are 'worth a manual check', never a confirmed verdict. Revocation checking is off by default and never on a per-tick poll path.

nodes.label: Degrade to Unknown, Never Fabricate
nodes.rationale: A denied registry key, an absent WMI namespace, or an unsupported sensor means the feature shows 'Unknown' or hides its section/card entirely — never a guessed or zeroed-out value presented as real.

nodes.label: Prefer Known Windows Tool over Raw Interop
nodes.rationale: schtasks/sc/vssadmin/fsutil/defrag/tracert/powercfg/netsh are shelled out to and their text output parsed via one shared ToolRunner (timeout kill is always entire process tree) rather than reimplementing via COM/registry/native structs. Raw P/Invoke is reserved for cases with no tool or WMI class at all, always wrapped to degrade gracefully rather than throw or hang.

nodes.label: CategorySampler (One Category per Tick)
nodes.rationale: Performance counters are read one category per tick, never one PerformanceCounter object per value — every raw NextValue() re-reads the entire category. The counter-per-instance ProcessPerfCounterService cost 4-9 seconds per tick on the ~350-instance Process category; HardwareMonitorService's ~130 individual counters cost ~70ms of every 1-second tick. Value parity is verified by running old and new implementations simultaneously and diffing snapshots.

nodes.label: Settings JSON Persistence Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every persisted setting is a small JSON file under AppPaths.SettingsDirectory (%AppData%\TaskManagerPlus, or a Settings folder next to the exe in portable mode) that fails silently to its type's defaults on a missing or corrupt file.

nodes.label: Rules Engine Health Check
nodes.rationale: The Summary Health Check is driven by RulesEngineService reading JSON rule packs (metric-bag conditions plus presentation metadata, no embedded scripting engine) seeded from a built-in pack, instead of a hardcoded if chain — new findings are added as rules, and HealthIssue is the one finding shape rendered everywhere (Health Check card, Troubleshoot, reports, evidence bundles).

nodes.label: Change Journal + Read-Only Mode Convention
nodes.rationale: Every system-mutating action appends an undoable entry to ChangeJournalService's change-journal.jsonl and respects ReadOnlyModeService's app-wide switch in its command's CanExecute. A remediation action shows its literal command line before running, offers a dry-run where one exists, and offers a restore point plus reg export before a risky change — copy this shape for any new mutating action.

nodes.label: StressTestSafetyMonitor (Always-On, No Opt-Out)
nodes.rationale: Because the stress-test suite loads CPU/GPU/memory/disk for real, every sample runs through an unconditional, unthrottled temperature-ceiling abort check that no setting can disable (only thresholds move). Any future feature that drives real hardware load on demand must follow this same always-on-safety-monitor shape rather than relying on the user-configured duration.

nodes.label: Typography and Spacing Tokens
nodes.rationale: Views once carried 1,889 hardcoded FontSize values across 18 distinct sizes, 179 Margin values and 11 CornerRadius values; collapsed onto a 7-step type scale plus spacing/radius tokens with real consumers. Unlike palette brushes these are StaticResource-consumed doubles since they never change at runtime.

nodes.label: Target Framework Pin (net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0)
nodes.rationale: A bare net8.0-windows expands to net8.0-windows7.0, which matches none of SkiaSharp.Views.WPF's windows10 asset groups, so NuGet silently fell back to net462 SkiaSharp.Views.WPF, net452 GLWpfControl and .NET 2.0 OpenTK — the only symptom was cosmetic-looking NU1701 warnings. Naming 10.0.19041 selects the real net8.0 assets and sets the Windows 10 2004 floor; the Release output path therefore carries the full moniker.

nodes.label: Smart App Control Blocks Unsigned Builds
nodes.rationale: Smart App Control, if On, blocks locally-built unsigned exes from launching at all (instant crash, exit 0xE0434352). Signing with the dev-cert scripts fixes 'Unknown Publisher' but does not satisfy SAC, which blocks on reputation, not signature validity — turning SAC off (one-way without a full OS reset) is the only real fix.

nodes.label: Whole-App Elevation (requireAdministrator)
nodes.rationale: The whole app runs elevated via app.manifest rather than elevating per-action, so ending other users' processes and controlling services just work without extra prompts — at the cost of one UAC prompt per launch and an instance that can't be killed from a non-elevated shell.

nodes.label: CPU Clock Derivation (Base x % Processor Performance)
nodes.rationale: Current clock speed is not directly exposed by Windows; it is computed the same way the real Task Manager does — read Win32_Processor.MaxClockSpeed once via WMI, then multiply by the % Processor Performance counter each tick (reflects turbo/throttling).

nodes.label: StartupApproved Flag Toggle
nodes.rationale: Startup enable/disable doesn't touch the registry Run value or move the shortcut — it flips the binary flag under Explorer\StartupApproved\Run (or \StartupApproved\StartupFolder) that Explorer itself checks, staying consistent with Explorer and the built-in Task Manager.

nodes.label: Sensor Monitoring via LibreHardwareMonitorLib
nodes.rationale: No reliable Windows API exists for temperature/fan/voltage/power, so SensorMonitorService is the one place the app takes this third-party dependency (LibreHardwareMonitorLib, MPL-2.0 — a different license family from the MIT project). Sensor names aren't standardized across vendors, so headline readings use a name-hint search, not an exact lookup.

nodes.label: ETW via logman/wpr + tracerpt (No TraceEvent)
nodes.rationale: Several Responsiveness-tab services need real-time kernel/ETW data but deliberately avoid the TraceEvent NuGet package: they shell out to logman/wpr to capture a short .etl, convert with tracerpt -of XML, and parse leniently (substring field matching) since the classic MOF-based layout tracerpt renders isn't a stable public contract. A non-matching build parses zero events — an empty grid with an explanatory message, never a crash or fabricated numbers. Start/Stop-gated, tool presence checked first.

nodes.label: Nested Sub-ViewModel + Toggle Panel
nodes.rationale: Heavier mostly-self-contained feature blocks on the Events tab (EtwCaptureViewModel, ServicingLogsViewModel) are toggleable side panels with their own nested sub-ViewModel composed as plain properties, rather than flattening everything onto one giant tab ViewModel — the shape to use for the next large feature block belonging on an existing tab.

hyperedges.label: Honest-Data House Rules (never fabricate, flag not verdict, curated not authoritative)
